title: fix(windows): agent card selected_target.file emits native separators, breaking portable JSON contract
body:
## Observation (verified_current)

On native Windows (PowerShell), `ripr agent card --json` emits `selected_target.file` with native backslash separators. `agent_card_readiness_agrees_with_repair_target_admission` fails at `crates/ripr/tests/cli_smoke.rs:4019` with left `src\lib.rs` against right `src/lib.rs`. Reproduced identically on exact base `b0c9ff3` (detached worktree, no local changes), so this is inherited, not caused by in-flight work.

`windows-advisory.yml` runs the full workspace suite but always exits 0 (advisory). The required gate matrix is Linux, where the portable assertion holds, so this never blocks.

## Proposal

Machine-readable card output should use portable `/`-separated paths (the test already asserts this). Other emitters already normalize; only the card path leaks native separators. My recommendation is to normalize the card emitter and keep the test as is.

One question before a PR: should the fix also cover the sibling path fields in the same card envelope if they leak separators, or stay narrowly on `selected_target.file`?

## Notes

Found hands-on while triaging the #5336 span-projection lane; left out of that PR as a different semantic owner (agent card paths). Advisory runs use Git Bash while this repro is native PowerShell, so confirm which shell the advisory card path takes before assuming the advisory log shows it.
